grammarFocus: Passé composé with avoir and être

sentences.source: I went to the market yesterday morning.
She has already finished her homework.
We arrived at the station at noon.
They ate dinner at a restaurant last night.
He fell asleep on the sofa after the film.
When I was young, I used to play in the garden every day.
It was raining and the streets were empty.
She was reading a novel while he was cooking dinner.
They always drank coffee after lunch when they worked together.
The old house had a big oak tree in the courtyard.
I was walking home when I suddenly heard a strange noise.
While she was sleeping, her phone rang twice.
He used to cycle to work, but yesterday he took the bus.
We were eating when the power went out.
The children were playing outside when it started to snow.
Tomorrow I will wake up early and go for a run.
Next summer, she will travel to Spain with her family.
They will finish the project by Friday.
Will you come to the party on Saturday?
If you study hard, you will pass the exam.
Could you please open the window? It is very hot in here.
I would like a table for two, please.
If I had more time, I would learn to paint.
She would be happy if you called her more often.
We would travel around the world if we could.

grammarFocus: Subjonctif présent after expressions of necessity and emotion

sentences.source: It is important that you arrive on time.
I am glad that she can come to the party.
The teacher wants us to be quiet during the test.
It is a shame that he does not speak French.
We need you to finish this report before Monday.
The woman who lives next door is a doctor.
The book that I am reading is very interesting.
He is the colleague who helped me with my presentation.
The film that we watched last night was funny.
She has a friend who speaks five languages.
This is the film I told you about.
She is the student whose work impressed everyone.
He bought the car he had been dreaming of.
That is the restaurant whose menu changes every week.
I remember the day we met, whose memory still makes me smile.
The city where I grew up is on the coast.
I remember the year when everything changed.
Show me the office where you work every day.
The moment when she walked in, the room fell silent.
He returned to the village where his grandparents had lived.
I see the cat. — I see it.
She loves French films. — She loves them.
He will call his mother tonight. — He will call her tonight.
Do you know this song? — Yes, I know it.
They have invited us to their wedding.
I sent a postcard to my grandmother. — I sent her a postcard.
He talks to his friends every evening. — He talks to them every evening.
She gave the keys to the manager. — She gave him the keys.
Can you explain the rules to us, please?
I will write to you as soon as I arrive.
I only have ten euros left.
She only eats vegetables and fruit.
He spoke only a few words and then left.
There is only one train per day to that village.
We only see each other on weekends.
She listens to podcasts while commuting to work.
You can improve your French by speaking every day.
He answered the phone while eating his lunch.
By working together, we finished the task faster.
She hurt her ankle while playing tennis.
This café is more expensive than the one near the station.
She speaks French better than her brother.
It is the most beautiful painting I have ever seen.
The train is faster than the bus, but the bus is cheaper.
He is the least experienced member of the team.
If I spoke French perfectly, I would apply for that job in Paris.
If we had a car, we would visit them more often.
What would you do if you won the lottery?
If she studied more, she would get better grades.
If it were not raining, we would eat on the terrace.
I wake up at seven and get dressed quickly.
They met at university and fell in love.
She is interested in contemporary art.
We are looking forward to the holidays.
He remembered the address just in time.
By the time you arrive, I will have already cooked dinner.
She will have finished her degree by next June.
Once they will have signed the contract, we can start.
He will have lived in France for ten years by next spring.
Will you have read the report before the meeting tomorrow?
She had already left when I arrived at the café.
He ate the cake that his mother had made the day before.
They had never visited Paris before that trip.
I realized I had forgotten my wallet at home.
We had barely sat down when the concert began.
Do you go to the gym often? — Yes, I go there twice a week.
She has three brothers. — She has three of them.
Are you thinking about the trip? — Yes, I am thinking about it.
Do you want some bread? — No, thank you, I don't want any.
He has lived in Lyon for three years. — He has lived there for three years.
He said, 'I am tired.' → He said that he was tired.
She told me, 'I will call you tomorrow.' → She told me she would call me the next day.
They asked, 'Where does she live?' → They asked where she lived.
The guide explained, 'The museum closes at six.' → The guide explained that the museum closed at six.
My friend said, 'I have never tried snails.' → My friend said he had never tried snails.
